15: #[derive(Clone)]
16: pub struct Gateway {
17:     pub config: Config,
18:     pub db_pool: SqlitePool,
19:     pub internal_client: InternalClient,
20:     pub rate_limiter: Arc<RateLimiter>,
21: }
22: 
23: impl Gateway {
24:     pub fn new(
25:         config: Config,
26:         db_pool: SqlitePool,
27:     ) -> Result<Self, Vec<crate::config::ConfigError>> {
28:         let internal_client = InternalClient::new(
29:             config.internal_api_base.clone(),
30:             config.internal_api_key.clone(),
31:         )
32:         .map_err(|e| vec![e])?;
33: 
34:         let rate_limiter = if config.rate_limit_enabled {
35:             Arc::new(RateLimiter::new())
36:         } else {
37:             Arc::new(RateLimiter::disabled())
38:         };
39: 
40:         Ok(Self {
41:             config,
42:             db_pool,
43:             internal_client,
44:             rate_limiter,
45:         })
46:     }
47: 
48:     /// Run an already-authenticated tools/call: resolve the authoritative
49:     /// grant, dispatch to the tool, and record the invocation in the local
50:     /// audit log.
51:     ///
52:     /// Audit recording is best-effort: a failed audit insert is logged as an
53:     /// operational error and never replaces an already-completed tool response.
54:     /// Returning failure would encourage a client to repeat a mutation that
55:     /// already succeeded.
56:     pub async fn handle_authorized_tool_call(
57:         &self,
58:         request_id: &str,
59:         token_result: &TokenValidationResult,
60:         message: &serde_json::Value,
61:     ) -> axum::http::Response<axum::body::Body> {
62:         // Extract tool name and params
63:         let tool_name = message
64:             .get("params")
65:             .and_then(|p| p.get("name"))
66:             .and_then(|n| n.as_str())
67:             .unwrap_or("");
68: 
69:         let params = message
70:             .get("params")
71:             .and_then(|p| p.get("arguments"))
72:             .cloned()
73:             .unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({}));
74: 
75:         let auth_strength = token_result.auth_strength.to_string();
76: 
77:         // Resolve the authoritative grant from CommonCal core (source of truth).
78:         let grant = match self
79:             .internal_client
80:             .get_mcp_grant(token_result.user_id, &token_result.oauth_client_id)
81:             .await
82:         {
83:             Ok(Some(resp)) => McpGrant::from(resp),
84:             Ok(None) => {
85:                 self.record_audit(&AuditRecord {
86:                     request_id,
87:                     user_id: token_result.user_id,
88:                     client_id: &token_result.oauth_client_id,
89:                     grant_id: None,
90:                     tool: tool_name,
91:                     resource_ids: None,
92:                     auth_result: "denied",
93:                     scope: None,
94:                     auth_strength: &auth_strength,
95:                     latency_ms: 0,
96:                     result_type: "denied",
97:                     operation_id: None,
98:                 })
99:                 .await;
100:                 return axum::http::Response::builder()
101:                     .status(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN)
102:                     .header("content-type", "application/json")
103:                     .body(axum::body::Body::from(
104:                         serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
105:                             "jsonrpc": "2.0",
106:                             "id": message.get("id"),
107:                             "error": {
108:                                 "code": -2003,
109:                                 "message": "no MCP grant found",
110:                             },
111:                         }))
112:                         .unwrap(),
113:                     ))
114:                     .unwrap();
115:             }
116:             Err(e) => {
117:                 self.record_audit(&AuditRecord {
118:                     request_id,
119:                     user_id: token_result.user_id,
120:                     client_id: &token_result.oauth_client_id,
121:                     grant_id: None,
122:                     tool: tool_name,
123:                     resource_ids: None,
124:                     auth_result: "denied",
125:                     scope: None,
126:                     auth_strength: &auth_strength,
127:                     latency_ms: 0,
128:                     result_type: "error",
129:                     operation_id: None,
130:                 })
131:                 .await;
132:                 return axum::http::Response::builder()
133:                     .status(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)
134:                     .header("content-type", "application/json")
135:                     .body(axum::body::Body::from(
136:                         serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
137:                             "jsonrpc": "2.0",
138:                             "id": message.get("id"),
139:                             "error": {
140:                                 "code": -2005,
141:                                 "message": format!("grant resolution failed: {}", e),
142:                             },
143:                         }))
144:                         .unwrap(),
145:                     ))
146:                     .unwrap();
147:             }
148:         };
149: 
150:         // Build the authorized context and dispatch to the tool.
151:         let context = AuthorizedToolContext {
152:             token: token_result,
153:             grant: &grant,
154:             internal_client: &self.internal_client,
155:         };
156: 
157:         let started = std::time::Instant::now();
158:         match tools::dispatch(&context, tool_name, params).await {
159:             Ok(response) => {
160:                 self.record_audit(&AuditRecord {
161:                     request_id,
162:                     user_id: token_result.user_id,
163:                     client_id: &token_result.oauth_client_id,
164:                     grant_id: Some(&grant.grant_id),
165:                     tool: tool_name,
166:                     resource_ids: None,
167:                     auth_result: "allowed",
168:                     scope: None,
169:                     auth_strength: &auth_strength,
170:                     latency_ms: started.elapsed().as_millis() as i64,
171:                     result_type: "success",
172:                     operation_id: None,
173:                 })
174:                 .await;
175:                 response
176:             }
177:             Err(e) => {
178:                 let (auth_result, result_type) = match e {
179:                     ToolError::Unauthorized(_) | ToolError::Forbidden(_) => ("denied", "denied"),
180:                     _ => ("allowed", "error"),

182:                 self.record_audit(&AuditRecord {
183:                     request_id,
184:                     user_id: token_result.user_id,
185:                     client_id: &token_result.oauth_client_id,
186:                     grant_id: Some(&grant.grant_id),
187:                     tool: tool_name,
188:                     resource_ids: None,
189:                     auth_result,
190:                     scope: None,
191:                     auth_strength: &auth_strength,
192:                     latency_ms: started.elapsed().as_millis() as i64,
193:                     result_type,
194:                     operation_id: None,
195:                 })
196:                 .await;
197:                 let mcp_error = e.to_mcp_error(message.get("id"));
198:                 axum::http::Response::builder()
199:                     .status(StatusCode::OK)
200:                     .header("content-type", "application/json")
201:                     .body(axum::body::Body::from(
202:                         serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({
203:                             "jsonrpc": "2.0",

205:                             "error": {
206:                             "code": mcp_error["error"]["code"],

208:                             },

212:                     .unwrap()
213:             }

63:     Discovery(String),

65:     Jwks(String),

70: /// Discover the `jwks_uri` from the authorization-server metadata.
71: pub async fn discover_jwks_uri(http: &reqwest::Client, issuer: &str) -> Result<String, JwtError> {
72:     let url = format!("{issuer}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server");
73:     let meta: Value = http
74:         .get(&url)
75:         .send()
76:         .await
77:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Transport(e.to_string()))?
78:         .error_for_status()
79:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Discovery(e.to_string()))?
80:         .json()
81:         .await
82:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Discovery(e.to_string()))?;
83:     meta.get("jwks_uri")
84:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
85:         .map(|s| s.to_string())
86:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Discovery("metadata missing jwks_uri".into()))

89: /// Fetch the JWKS document.
90: pub async fn fetch_jwks(http: &reqwest::Client, jwks_uri: &str) -> Result<Value, JwtError> {
91:     http.get(jwks_uri)
92:         .send()
93:         .await
94:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Transport(e.to_string()))?
95:         .error_for_status()
96:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Jwks(e.to_string()))?
97:         .json()
98:         .await
99:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Jwks(e.to_string()))
100: }
101: 
102: /// Convert an RSA JWK (n, e) into a jsonwebtoken DecodingKey.
103: ///
104: /// Mirrors the proven pattern in `mcp-server/src/oauth.rs`: decode base64url
105: /// big-endian integers, pad the modulus to a multiple of 128 bytes, build the
106: /// RSA public key, and export to SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM.
107: fn jwk_to_decoding_key(jwk: &Value) -> Result<DecodingKey, JwtError> {
108:     if jwk.get("kty").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) != Some("RSA") {
109:         return Err(JwtError::Jwks("unsupported key type, expected RSA".into()));
110:     }
111:     let n = jwk
112:         .get("n")
113:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
114:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks("missing n".into()))?;
115:     let e = jwk
116:         .get("e")
117:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
118:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks("missing e".into()))?;
119:     let engine = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD;
120:     let n_bytes = engine
121:         .decode(n)
122:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("bad n: {err}")))?;
123:     let e_bytes = engine
124:         .decode(e)
125:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("bad e: {err}")))?;
126: 
127:     let key_size_bytes = n_bytes.len().div_ceil(128) * 128;
128:     let n_padded = if n_bytes.len() < key_size_bytes {
129:         let mut padded = vec![0u8; key_size_bytes - n_bytes.len()];
130:         padded.extend_from_slice(&n_bytes);
131:         padded
132:     } else {
133:         n_bytes
134:     };
135: 
136:     let n_big = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&n_padded);
137:     let e_big = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&e_bytes);
138:     let rsa_pub = rsa::RsaPublicKey::new(n_big, e_big)
139:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("rsa key: {err}")))?;
140:     let pem = rsa_pub
141:         .to_public_key_pem(rsa::pkcs8::LineEnding::default())
142:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("pem: {err}")))?;
143:     DecodingKey::from_rsa_pem(pem.as_bytes())
144:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("decoding key: {err}")))
145: }
146: 
147: /// Validate a JWT access token against the issuer and the exact resource audience.
148: ///
149: /// Checks: signature (via discovery JWKS), `iss`, `aud` (contains the exact
150: /// resource), `exp`, and extracts the standard claims.
151: pub async fn validate_access_token(
152:     http: &reqwest::Client,
153:     token: &str,
154:     issuer: &str,
155:     resource: &str,
156: ) -> Result<AccessClaims, JwtError> {
157:     let jwks_uri = discover_jwks_uri(http, issuer).await?;
158:     let jwks = fetch_jwks(http, &jwks_uri).await?;
159:     let keys = jwks
160:         .get("keys")
161:         .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
162:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks("no keys".into()))?;
163: 
164:     // Decode header to find kid + alg.
165:     let header = jsonwebtoken::decode_header(token)
166:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Token(format!("header: {err}")))?;
167:     let kid = header.kid;
168:     let alg = header.alg;
169: 
170:     let jwk = keys
171:         .iter()
172:         .find(|k| k.get("kid").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) == kid.as_deref())
173:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks(format!("no key for kid {kid:?}")))?;
174: 
175:     let decoding_key = jwk_to_decoding_key(jwk)?;
176: 
177:     let mut validation = Validation::new(alg);
178:     validation.set_issuer(&[issuer]);
179:     validation.set_audience(&[resource]);
180:     validation.leeway = 30;
181: 
182:     let data = jsonwebtoken::decode::<AccessClaims>(token, &decoding_key, &validation)
183:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Token(err.to_string()))?;
184:     Ok(data.claims)
185: }

557:     /// Parse a UTC timestamp (ISO 8601 or Unix epoch) to i64 seconds.
558:     fn parse_ts(s: &str) -> Option<i64> {
559:         if let Ok(ts) = s.parse::<i64>() {
560:             return Some(ts);
561:         }
562:         chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(s)
563:             .ok()
564:             .map(|dt| dt.timestamp())
565:     }

567:     /// Compute availability slots for a calendar in [from, to].
568:     /// A slot is "busy" if an event overlaps it, otherwise "free".
569:     /// Slots are 1-hour blocks aligned to the hour.
570:     async fn compute_availability(
571:         &self,
572:         calendar_id: i64,
573:         from: &str,
574:         to: &str,
575:     ) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
576:         let from_ts = Self::parse_ts(from).unwrap_or(0);
577:         let to_ts = Self::parse_ts(to).unwrap_or(0);
578:         let events: Vec<Event> = {
579:             let st = self.inner.read().await;
580:             st.events
581:                 .values()
582:                 .filter(|e| e.calendar_id == calendar_id)
583:                 .cloned()
584:                 .collect()
585:         };
586: 
587:         let mut slots = Vec::new();
588:         let mut t = from_ts;
589:         while t < to_ts {
590:             let slot_end = (t + 3600).min(to_ts);
591:             let busy = events.iter().any(|e| {
592:                 e.start_utc.is_some_and(|s| s < slot_end) && e.end_utc.is_some_and(|en| en > t)
593:             });
594:             slots.push(serde_json::json!({
595:                 "start": t,
596:                 "end": slot_end,
597:                 "status": if busy { "busy" } else { "free" },
598:             }));
599:             t = slot_end;
600:         }
601:         slots
602:     }

615:         &self,

618:         to: &str,

630:                     || e.end_utc.is_some_and(|en| en >= from_ts && en <= to_ts)

646:         results.sort_by_key(|e| e.start_utc.unwrap_or(0));

856:     /// Look up a handoff from the auth server's private API.
857:     async fn lookup_interaction(&self, handoff: &str) -> Result<InteractionView, String> {
858:         let url = format!(
859:             "{}/internal/interactions/{}",

867:             .send()
868:             .await
869:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
870:         let status = resp.status();
871:         if !status.is_success() {
872:             let body = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
873:             tracing::error!(status = %status, body = %body, "lookup_interaction failed");
874:             return Err(format!("interaction lookup failed: {status} {body}"));
875:         }
876:         let body = resp.text().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

882:     /// Decide a handoff (login/consent/deny) via the auth server's private API.
883:     /// `subject` is the authenticated CommonCal user id (the identity authority
884:     /// is CommonCal; the auth server binds the provider grant to this subject
885:     /// rather than a hardcoded value). Returns the resume URL.
886:     ///
887:     /// Honors the lab bridge-failure test hook: if armed, this call fails
888:     /// (simulating a bridge timeout) and the hook decrements, so a retry
889:     /// succeeds — proving grant-first / bridge-second idempotent retry.
890:     async fn decide_interaction(
891:         &self,
892:         handoff: &str,
893:         kind: &str,
894:         subject: Option<i64>,
895:     ) -> Result<String, String> {
896:         // Lab test hook: simulate a bridge failure on the next CONSENT decide
897:         // call(s). Only consent decisions are affected — the grant-first /
898:         // bridge-second ordering is a consent-path property, and login decisions
899:         // must not be disrupted (they precede the grant write).
900:         if kind == "consent" {
901:             let mut st = self.inner.write().await;
902:             if st.decide_fail_remaining > 0 {
903:                 st.decide_fail_remaining -= 1;
904:                 tracing::warn!("simulating bridge decide failure (test hook)");
905:                 return Err("simulated bridge timeout (test hook)".to_string());
906:             }
907:         }
908: 
909:         let url = format!(
910:             "{}/internal/interactions/{}",
911:             self.auth_private_base,
912:             urlencoding::encode(handoff)
913:         );
914:         let mut body = serde_json::json!({ "kind": kind });
915:         if let Some(sub) = subject {
916:             body["subject"] = serde_json::json!(sub);
917:         }
918:         let resp = self
919:             .http
920:             .put(&url)
921:             .header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {}", self.bridge_key))
922:             .json(&body)
923:             .send()
924:             .await
925:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
926:         let status = resp.status();
927:         if !status.is_success() {
928:             let text = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
929:             tracing::error!(status = %status, text = %text, "decide_interaction failed");
930:             return Err(format!("interaction decide failed: {status} {text}"));
931:         }
932:         let result: serde_json::Value = resp.json().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
933:         result
934:             .get("resumeUrl")
935:             .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
936:             .map(|s| s.to_string())
937:             .ok_or_else(|| "decide response missing resumeUrl".to_string())
938:     }
939: }

954: /// GET /consent?handoff=...
955: ///
956: /// If the interaction prompt is "login" and the user has a session, decide
957: /// login immediately (redirect to resume URL). If the prompt is "consent",
958: /// render the consent page. If no session, redirect to /login.
959: async fn consent_page(
960:     State(state): State<AppState>,
961:     Query(q): Query<ConsentQuery>,
962:     headers: HeaderMap,
963: ) -> Response {
964:     let handoff = match &q.handoff {
965:         Some(h) if !h.is_empty() => h.clone(),
966:         _ => {
967:             return (
968:                 StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
969:                 Json(serde_json::json!({"error": "missing_handoff"})),
970:             )
971:                 .into_response();
972:         }
973:     };
974: 
975:     // Look up the interaction from the auth server.
976:     let view = match state.lookup_interaction(&handoff).await {
977:         Ok(v) => v,
978:         Err(e) => {
979:             return (
980:                 StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
981:                 Json(serde_json::json!({"error": e})),
982:             )
983:                 .into_response();
984:         }
985:     };
986: 
987:     // Check if the user has a session.
988:     let session_token = extract_session_cookie(&headers);
989:     let user_id = match &session_token {
990:         Some(t) => state.get_session(t).await,
991:         None => None,
992:     };
993: 
994:     // If no session, redirect to login with a continue param.
995:     let continue_url = format!("/consent?handoff={}", urlencoding::encode(&handoff));
996:     let (session_token, user_id) = match (&session_token, user_id) {
997:         (Some(t), Some(uid)) => (t.clone(), uid),
998:         _ => {
999:             let location = format!("/login?continue={}", urlencoding::encode(&continue_url));
1000:             return (StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, [(header::LOCATION, location)]).into_response();
1001:         }
1002:     };
1003: 
1004:     // If the prompt is "login", decide login immediately (user is authenticated).
1005:     if view.prompt == "login" {

1010:             Ok(resume_url) => {
1011:                 return (StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, [(header::LOCATION, resume_url)]).into_response();
1012:             }
1013:             Err(e) => {
1014:                 return (
1015:                     StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
1016:                     Json(serde_json::json!({"error": e})),
1017:                 )

1031:         let html = format!(
1032:             r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
1033: <html lang="en">
1034: <head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>CommonCal — Authorize</title>
1035: <style>body{{font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;max-width:480px;margin:2rem auto;padding:0 1rem}}

1233: async fn consent_decision(
1234:     State(state): State<AppState>,
1235:     headers: HeaderMap,
1236:     body: axum::body::Bytes,
1237: ) -> Response {
1238:     let params = parse_form(&body);
1239:     let handoff = match params.get("handoff").cloned() {
1240:         Some(h) => h,
1241:         None => return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "missing handoff").into_response(),
1242:     };
1243:     let csrf = match params.get("csrf").cloned() {
1244:         Some(c) => c,
1245:         None => return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "missing csrf").into_response(),
1246:     };
1247:     let decision = match params.get("decision").cloned() {
1248:         Some(d) if d == "approve" || d == "deny" => d,
1249:         _ => return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "invalid decision").into_response(),
1250:     };
1251: 
1252:     // Validate session.
1253:     let session_token = match extract_session_cookie(&headers) {
1254:         Some(t) => t,
1255:         None => return (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, "no session").into_response(),
1256:     };
1257:     let user_id = match state.get_session(&session_token).await {
1258:         Some(id) => id,
1259:         None => return (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, "invalid session").into_response(),
1260:     };
1261: 
1262:     // Validate CSRF.
1263:     if !state.validate_csrf(&csrf, &session_token).await {
1264:         return (StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "invalid csrf token").into_response();
1265:     }
1266:     state.consume_csrf(&csrf).await;
1267: 
1268:     // Look up the interaction to get the requested scopes and client ID.
1269:     let view = match state.lookup_interaction(&handoff).await {
1270:         Ok(v) => v,
1271:         Err(e) => return (StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY, e).into_response(),
1272:     };
1273: 
1274:     if decision == "deny" {
1275:         match state
1276:             .decide_interaction(&handoff, "deny", Some(user_id))
1277:             .await
1278:         {
1279:             Ok(resume_url) => {
1280:                 return (StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, [(header::LOCATION, resume_url)]).into_response();
1281:             }
1282:             Err(e) => return (StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY, e).into_response(),
1283:         }
1284:     }
1285: 
1286:     // Approve: grant-first ordering.
1287:     // 1. Create the mcp_grant (in CommonCal's store).
1288:     // 2. Then decide consent via the auth server.
1289:     // If step 2 fails, the grant still exists (safe — user can revoke).
1290: 
1291:     // Determine which calendars the user owns (eligible calendars).
1292:     let calendars = state.list_calendars_for_user(user_id).await;
1293:     let allowed_ids: Vec<i64> = calendars.iter().map(|c| c.id).collect();
1294: 
1295:     // The granted scopes are the intersection of requested and catalog, computed
1296:     // by the auth server and returned in the handoff view. Record these (not the
1297:     // raw requested set) so the grant agrees with the JWT. Fall back to the
1298:     // requested set only if the view predates the grantedScopes field.
1299:     let granted_scopes = if view.granted_scopes.is_empty() {
1300:         view.requested_scopes.clone()
1301:     } else {
1302:         view.granted_scopes.clone()
1303:     };
1304: 
1305:     // Grant created. Now decide consent (grant-first: grant precedes consent).
1306:     state
1307:         .upsert_grant(user_id, &view.client_id, allowed_ids, granted_scopes)
1308:         .await;
1309:     match state
1310:         .decide_interaction(&handoff, "consent", Some(user_id))
1311:         .await
1312:     {
1313:         Ok(resume_url) => {
1314:             info!(user_id, client_id = %view.client_id, "consent approved, grant created");
1315:             (StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, [(header::LOCATION, resume_url)]).into_response()
1316:         }
1317:         Err(e) => {
1318:             // Grant exists but consent failed. This is safe (grant-first).
1319:             error!(error = %e, "consent decision failed after grant creation");
1320:             (StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY, e).into_response()
1321:         }
1322:     }
1323: }

57: function b64urlDecode(str) {
58:   return Buffer.from(str, "base64url");
59: }
60: 
61: function b64urlJson(obj) {
62:   return b64urlEncode(JSON.stringify(obj));
63: }
64: 
65: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66: // RSA key + JWK + RS256 JWT
67: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
68: 
69: /**
70:  * Generate an RSA key pair and expose the public key as a JWK (n, e) plus a
71:  * signing function. The private key never leaves this module.
72:  */
73: function createSigningKey(kid) {
74:   const { publicKey, privateKey } = crypto.generateKeyPairSync("rsa", {
75:     modulusLength: 2048,
76:     publicKeyEncoding: { type: "spki", format: "pem" },
77:     privateKeyEncoding: { type: "pkcs8", format: "pem" },
78:   });
79: 
80:   // Extract n and e from the SPKI public key.
81:   const keyObj = crypto.createPublicKey(publicKey);
82:   const jwk = keyObj.export({ format: "jwk" });
83: 
84:   return {
85:     kid,
86:     jwk: {
87:       kty: "RSA",
88:       n: jwk.n,
89:       e: jwk.e,
90:       use: "sig",
91:       alg: "RS256",
92:       kid,
93:     },
94:     sign(payload) {
95:       const signer = crypto.createSign("RSA-SHA256");
96:       signer.update(payload);
97:       signer.end();
98:       // Output encoding is base64url; the signature format is DER (PKCS#1 v1.5),
99:       // which is what RSA-SHA256 produces by default.
100:       return signer.sign(privateKey, "base64url");
101:     },
102:   };
103: }
104: 
105: /**
106:  * Sign a JWT (RS256) with the given claims and signing key.
107:  */
108: function signJwt(claims, signingKey) {
109:   const header = { alg: "RS256", typ: "JWT", kid: signingKey.kid };
110:   const signingInput = `${b64urlJson(header)}.${b64urlJson(claims)}`;
111:   const signature = signingKey.sign(signingInput);
112:   return `${signingInput}.${signature}`;
113: }
114: 
115: /**
116:  * Verify an RS256 JWT signature against a JWK. Returns true if valid.
117:  */
118: function verifyJwtSignature(jwt, jwk) {
119:   const parts = jwt.split(".");
120:   if (parts.length !== 3) return false;
121:   const [headerB64, payloadB64, signatureB64] = parts;
122:   let header;
123:   try {
124:     header = JSON.parse(b64urlDecode(headerB64).toString("utf8"));
125:   } catch {
126:     return false;
127:   }
128:   if (header.alg !== "RS256") return false;
129:   if (jwk.kty !== "RSA" || !jwk.n || !jwk.e) return false;
130: 
131:   // Reconstruct the RSA public key from the JWK (n, e). Node handles the
132:   // modulus padding internally for the JWK->key conversion.
133:   let publicKey;
134:   try {
135:     publicKey = crypto.createPublicKey({
136:       key: { kty: "RSA", n: jwk.n, e: jwk.e },
137:       format: "jwk",
138:     });
139:   } catch {
140:     return false;
141:   }
142: 
143:   const verifier = crypto.createVerify("RSA-SHA256");
144:   verifier.update(`${headerB64}.${payloadB64}`);
145:   verifier.end();
146:   try {
147:     // Pass the signature as a Buffer (default 'buffer' format).
148:     return verifier.verify(publicKey, b64urlDecode(signatureB64));
149:   } catch {
150:     return false;
151:   }
152: }
153: 
154: /**
155:  * Decode a JWT payload (no signature verification). Returns the claims object
156:  * or null.
157:  */
158: function decodeJwtPayload(jwt) {
159:   const parts = jwt.split(".");
160:   if (parts.length !== 3) return null;
161:   try {
162:     return JSON.parse(b64urlDecode(parts[1]).toString("utf8"));
163:   } catch {
164:     return null;
165:   }
166: }
167: 
168: /**
169:  * Decode a JWT header (no signature verification). Returns the header object
170:  * or null.
171:  */
172: function decodeJwtHeader(jwt) {
173:   const parts = jwt.split(".");
174:   if (parts.length !== 3) return null;
175:   try {
176:     return JSON.parse(b64urlDecode(parts[0]).toString("utf8"));
177:   } catch {
178:     return null;
179:   }
180: }
181: 
182: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
183: // PKCE S256
184: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
185: 
186: /**
187:  * Compute the S256 code challenge for a verifier (RFC 7636).
188:  */
189: function s256Challenge(verifier) {
190:   return b64urlEncode(crypto.createHash("sha256").update(verifier).digest());
191: }
192: 
193: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
194: // The mock OAuth provider
195: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
196: 
197: /**
198:  * A self-contained mock OAuth authorization server.
199:  *
200:  * @param {object} opts
201:  * @param {string} opts.issuer      The issuer base URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:PORT).
202:  * @param {string} opts.resource    The exact MCP resource / audience.
203:  * @param {string} opts.redirect    The admitted loopback redirect URI.
204:  * @param {string} [opts.kid]       The signing key id.
205:  */
206: class MockOAuthProvider {
207:   constructor({ issuer, resource, redirect, kid = "mcp-acceptance-rs256" }) {
208:     this.issuer = issuer.replace(/\/$/, "");
209:     this.resource = resource;
210:     this.redirect = redirect;
211:     this.signingKey = createSigningKey(kid);
212: 
213:     // Stores.
214:     this.clients = new Map(); // client_id -> client metadata
215:     this.codes = new Map(); // code -> { client_id, redirect_uri, challenge, scope, sub, used }
216:     this.tokens = new Map(); // jti -> { client_id, sub, scope, aud, exp, iat }
217:     this.grants = new Map(); // `${sub}:${client_id}` -> grant
218: 
219:     this.clientSeq = 0;
220:   }
221: 
222:   // -- DCR ------------------------------------------------------------------
223: 
224:   /**
225:    * Handle a DCR (RFC 7591) registration request. Mirrors the lab's DCR
226:    * policy (slice1-lab/auth-server/src/server.mjs validateRegisteredMetadata):
227:    * exactly one loopback redirect, grant_types [authorization_code,
228:    * refresh_token], response_types [code], token_endpoint_auth_method none.
229:    *
230:    * @returns {{status: number, body: object}}
231:    */
232:   handleRegister(body) {
233:     const redirectUris = body.redirect_uris;
234:     if (!Array.isArray(redirectUris) || redirectUris.length !== 1) {
235:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_redirect_uris" } };
236:     }
237:     if (redirectUris[0] !== this.redirect) {
238:       return {
239:         status: 400,
240:         body: {
241:           error: "invalid_redirect_uri",
242:           error_description: `only the admitted loopback ${this.redirect} is allowed`,
243:         },
244:       };
245:     }
246:     const grantTypes = Array.isArray(body.grant_types) ? [...body.grant_types].sort() : [];
247:     if (
248:       JSON.stringify(grantTypes) !==
249:       JSON.stringify(["authorization_code", "refresh_token"])
250:     ) {
251:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant_types" } };
252:     }
253:     const responseTypes = Array.isArray(body.response_types) ? body.response_types : [];
254:     if (responseTypes.length !== 1 || responseTypes[0] !== "code") {
255:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_response_types" } };
256:     }
257:     if (body.token_endpoint_auth_method !== "none") {
258:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_token_endpoint_auth_method" } };
259:     }
260: 
261:     this.clientSeq += 1;
262:     const client_id = `mcp-acceptance-client-${this.clientSeq}`;
263:     const client = {
264:       client_id,
265:       client_name: body.client_name ?? "mcp-acceptance",
266:       redirect_uris: [this.redirect],
267:       grant_types: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
268:       response_types: ["code"],
269:       token_endpoint_auth_method: "none",
270:       scope: body.scope ?? SCOPE_CATALOG.join(" "),
271:     };
272:     this.clients.set(client_id, client);
273:     return { status: 201, body: client };
274:   }
275: 
276:   // -- Authorization --------------------------------------------------------
277: 
278:   /**
279:    * Handle an authorization request. In the mock, login + consent are
280:    * auto-approved (the lab's stub adapter / CommonCal consent is the identity
281:    * authority; the mock stands in for it). It issues an authorization code
282:    * bound to the client, redirect URI, PKCE challenge, scope, and subject.
283:    *
284:    * @param {object} params  URLSearchParams of the authorization request.
285:    * @returns {{status: number, body: object, location?: string}}
286:    */
287:   handleAuthorize(params) {
288:     const client_id = params.get("client_id");
289:     const client = this.clients.get(client_id);
290:     if (!client) {
291:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "unknown_client" } };
292:     }
293:     const redirect_uri = params.get("redirect_uri");
294:     if (redirect_uri !== this.redirect) {
295:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_redirect_uri" } };
296:     }
297:     const response_type = params.get("response_type");
298:     if (response_type !== "code") {
299:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "unsupported_response_type" } };
300:     }
301:     const code_challenge = params.get("code_challenge");
302:     const code_challenge_method = params.get("code_challenge_method");
303:     if (!code_challenge || code_challenge_method !== "S256") {
304:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_request", error_description: "S256 PKCE required" } };
305:     }
306:     const scope = params.get("scope") ?? "";
307:     const state = params.get("state") ?? "";
308: 
309:     // The subject is a CommonCal user id (numeric). The mock stands in for
310:     // CommonCal's identity authority and binds the fixed lab subject "1".
311:     const sub = "1";
312: 
313:     const code = `mcp-acceptance-code-${crypto.randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`;
314:     this.codes.set(code, {
315:       client_id,
316:       redirect_uri,
317:       challenge: code_challenge,
318:       scope,
319:       sub,
320:       used: false,
321:     });
322: 
323:     const location = `${this.redirect}?code=${encodeURIComponent(code)}&state=${encodeURIComponent(state)}`;
324:     return { status: 302, body: {}, location };
325:   }
326: 
327:   // -- Token ----------------------------------------------------------------
328: 
329:   /**
330:    * Handle a token exchange (Authorization Code + S256 PKCE). Verifies the
331:    * code, the PKCE verifier, and the redirect URI, then issues a JWT access
332:    * token with the standard claim contract.
333:    *
334:    * @param {object} params  URLSearchParams of the token request.
335:    * @returns {{status: number, body: object}}
336:    */
337:   handleToken(params) {
338:     const grant_type = params.get("grant_type");
339:     if (grant_type !== "authorization_code") {
340:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "unsupported_grant_type" } };
341:     }
342:     const code = params.get("code");
343:     const entry = this.codes.get(code);
344:     if (!entry) {
345:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "unknown or expired code" } };
346:     }
347:     if (entry.used) {
348:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "code already redeemed" } };
349:     }
350:     const client_id = params.get("client_id");
351:     if (client_id !== entry.client_id) {
352:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "client_id mismatch" } };
353:     }
354:     const redirect_uri = params.get("redirect_uri");
355:     if (redirect_uri !== entry.redirect_uri) {
356:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "redirect_uri mismatch" } };
357:     }
358:     const code_verifier = params.get("code_verifier");
359:     if (!code_verifier) {
360:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_request", error_description: "code_verifier required" } };
361:     }
362:     if (s256Challenge(code_verifier) !== entry.challenge) {
363:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "PKCE verifier mismatch" } };
364:     }
365: 
366:     entry.used = true;
367: 
368:     // The granted scopes are the intersection of requested and catalog
369:     // (slice1-lab/auth-server/src/server.mjs approvedResourceScopes).
370:     const requested = new Set(String(entry.scope).split(" ").filter(Boolean));
371:     const granted = SCOPE_CATALOG.filter((s) => requested.has(s));
372: 
373:     const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
374:     const jti = `mcp-acceptance-jti-${crypto.randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`;
375:     const claims = {
376:       iss: this.issuer,
377:       sub: entry.sub,
378:       aud: this.resource,
379:       exp: now + 300,
380:       iat: now,
381:       jti,
382:       client_id: entry.client_id,
383:       scope: granted.join(" "),
384:       amr: ["pwd"],
385:     };
386:     const access_token = signJwt(claims, this.signingKey);
387:     this.tokens.set(jti, {
388:       client_id: entry.client_id,
389:       sub: entry.sub,
390:       scope: granted.join(" "),
391:       aud: this.resource,
392:       exp: claims.exp,
393:       iat: now,
394:     });
395: 
396:     return {
397:       status: 200,
398:       body: {
399:         access_token,
400:         token_type: "Bearer",
401:         expires_in: 300,
402:         refresh_token: `mcp-acceptance-refresh-${crypto.randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`,
403:         scope: granted.join(" "),
404:       },
405:     };
406:   }
407: 
408:   // -- JWKS -----------------------------------------------------------------
409: 
410:   /**
411:    * The JWKS document (public key only).
412:    */
413:   jwks() {
414:     return { keys: [this.signingKey.jwk] };
415:   }
416: 
417:   // -- Token validation (resource-server side) ------------------------------
418: 
419:   /**
420:    * Validate an access token the way the production MCP server must:
421:    * signature (via JWKS), exact iss, exact aud, exp, and the standard claims.
422:    * Returns { ok, claims?, error? }.
423:    */
424:   validateAccessToken(token) {
425:     if (typeof token !== "string" || token.split(".").length !== 3) {
426:       return { ok: false, error: "malformed_token" };
427:     }
428:     const header = decodeJwtHeader(token);
429:     if (!header || header.alg !== "RS256") {
430:       return { ok: false, error: "unsupported_alg" };
431:     }
432:     const kid = header.kid;
433:     if (kid !== this.signingKey.kid) {
434:       return { ok: false, error: "unknown_kid" };
435:     }
436:     if (!verifyJwtSignature(token, this.signingKey.jwk)) {
437:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_signature" };
438:     }
439:     const claims = decodeJwtPayload(token);
440:     if (!claims) {
441:       return { ok: false, error: "malformed_payload" };
442:     }
443:     if (claims.iss !== this.issuer) {
444:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_issuer" };
445:     }
446:     const aud = Array.isArray(claims.aud) ? claims.aud : [claims.aud];
447:     if (!aud.includes(this.resource)) {
448:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_audience" };
449:     }
450:     const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
451:     if (typeof claims.exp !== "number" || claims.exp <= now) {
452:       return { ok: false, error: "token_expired" };
453:     }
454:     if (typeof claims.sub !== "string" || !/^\d+$/.test(claims.sub)) {
455:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_sub" };
456:     }
457:     if (typeof claims.client_id !== "string" || !this.clients.has(claims.client_id)) {
458:       return { ok: false, error: "unknown_client" };
459:     }
460:     return { ok: true, claims };
461:   }
462: 
463:   // -- Token minting (verification-only) ------------------------------------
464: 
465:   /**
466:    * Mint a token with the given claims, signed with the provider's key.
467:    *
468:    * This is a verification-only helper used by the Phase 0.4 security harness
469:    * to drive the negative token cases (wrong issuer / audience / expiry /
470:    * client) with a VALID signature, so each claim check is exercised in
471:    * isolation (not masked by a signature failure). It is NOT part of the
472:    * production contract and is only reachable through the mock's `/_test/*`
473:    * hooks.
474:    *
475:    * @param {object} claims  The claims to embed in the token.
476:    * @returns {string} A signed JWT.
477:    */
478:   mintToken(claims) {
479:     const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
480:     const fullClaims = {
481:       iss: this.issuer,
482:       sub: "1",
483:       aud: this.resource,
484:       exp: now + 300,
485:       iat: now,
486:       jti: `mcp-acceptance-mint-${crypto.randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`,
487:       client_id: "mcp-acceptance-client-1",
488:       scope: SCOPE_CATALOG.join(" "),
489:       amr: ["pwd"],
490:       ...claims,
491:     };
492:     return signJwt(fullClaims, this.signingKey);
493:   }
494: 
495:   // -- Grants ---------------------------------------------------------------
496: 
497:   /**
498:    * Create an active grant for (sub, client_id) with the given allowed
499:    * calendar ids and scopes. Mirrors slice1-lab/src/bin/commoncal.rs
500:    * upsert_grant (replace semantics).
501:    */
502:   upsertGrant(sub, client_id, allowedCalendarIds, scopes) {
503:     const key = `${sub}:${client_id}`;
504:     this.grants.set(key, {
505:       sub,
506:       client_id,
507:       allowed_calendar_ids: allowedCalendarIds,
508:       scopes,
509:       revoked: false,
510:     });
511:   }
512: 
513:   /**
514:    * Revoke the active grant for (sub, client_id).
515:    */
516:   revokeGrant(sub, client_id) {
517:     const key = `${sub}:${client_id}`;
518:     const grant = this.grants.get(key);
519:     if (grant) grant.revoked = true;
520:   }
521: 
522:   /**
523:    * Delete the grant for (sub, client_id) entirely (simulates a missing grant).
524:    */
525:   deleteGrant(sub, client_id) {
526:     this.grants.delete(`${sub}:${client_id}`);
527:   }
528: 
529:   /**
530:    * Get the active grant for (sub, client_id), or null.
531:    */
532:   getActiveGrant(sub, client_id) {
533:     const grant = this.grants.get(`${sub}:${client_id}`);
534:     if (!grant || grant.revoked) return null;
535:     return grant;
536:   }
537: }
538: 
539: module.exports = {
540:   MockOAuthProvider,
541:   SCOPE_CATALOG,
542:   EVIL_SCOPE,
543:   b64urlEncode,
544:   b64urlDecode,
545:   b64urlJson,
546:   createSigningKey,
547:   signJwt,
548:   verifyJwtSignature,
549:   decodeJwtPayload,
550:   decodeJwtHeader,
551:   s256Challenge,
552: };

(End of file - total 552 lines)

553:     /// is ambiguous core data and fails closed rather than selecting arbitrarily.

555:         &self,

310:     ///
311:     /// Tries `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414) first, then
312:     /// falls back to `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (OIDC). Verifies the
313:     /// returned `issuer` exactly matches the configured issuer.
314:     async fn discover_jwks_uri(&self, issuer: &str) -> Result<String, TokenError> {
315:         // Check cache first.
316:         {
317:             let cache = self.metadata_cache.lock().await;
318:             if let Some(entry) = cache.as_ref()
319:                 && entry.fetched_at.elapsed().as_secs() < METADATA_CACHE_TTL_SECS
320:             {

322:             }
323:         }

325:         // Try RFC 8414 location first, then OIDC fallback.
